correctness.rationale: For any directional normal, each coordinate-simplex support width is its coordinate range. Sorting coordinates yields an exact nonnegative sum of centered upper-level cut vectors with additive range cost; Euclidean triangle inequality forces a normalized-cost minimizing cut and its strict equality classification. Every cyclic tube either crosses the cut or lies within a monochromatic run; superadditivity of T(r)=r(r+1)/2 makes a cyclic single interval uniquely optimal at fixed cut size. The exact cut cost A_n+s(n-s) and derivative (z-A_n)/(2 z^(3/2)) yield all n formulas and equality cases, with a separate n=4 comparison. The packaged checker reproduces 2024 exact cut comparisons for n=3..10 and 4800 independent direction tests; finite checks are supplementary, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The standard n-cycle graph associahedron is a canonical highly structured polytope. The exact all-dimensional intrinsic Euclidean minimum-width invariant, complete classification and count of minimizing normal directions, and abrupt n=4 to n=5 change between singleton and balanced cyclic cuts answer a natural noncombinatorial metric question not resolved by existing inradius or graph-diameter values. The result is a complete structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite experiment or routine numerical improvement.
